clue.text: Not entirely accurate delivery to leave

parts.note: in cricket a delivery is one ball bowled
to park a car is to leave it somewhere

explanation.surface: A bowler's delivery that is a little off target and best left alone by the batsman.
explanation.walkthrough: A ballpark figure is a rough estimate.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a ballpark figure is an approximate one, close enough but not precise.

clue.text: Group of players pitted wits on ice now, with odd skids

indicators.note: something that skids slides about out of control, so these letters slither into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Rival skaters set against each other on an ice rink, their skates sliding oddly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pitted' looks like the contest of wits but belongs to the definition: the orchestra sits in a pit. The anagram signal is 'skids', not 'pitted'.
explanation.definitionFit: The woodwind section is a group of orchestral players, who at the opera or theatre sit in the orchestra pit.

clue.text: Help sought by narcissist leader in Trump, feckless individual I gathered

indicators.note: gathered means collected up together in a jumble, so these letters are rearranged
the leader of a word is its first letter, here taken from the word Trump

parts.note: taken as written
an individual is one, written as the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A dig at a vain politician who needs constant help from a hapless hanger-on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gathered' rearranges T (first of Trump), FECKLESS, I (one individual) and I together.
explanation.definitionFit: A narcissist keen on photographing themselves would want a pole that holds the phone at arm's length.

clue.text: Where behaviour refined on a trawler, say, having gathered in a lot of herring, perhaps?

indicators.note: having gathered means taking something into itself, so one word holds the other

parts.note: a crew on a trawler would be out catching fish
a school is a large group of fish such as herring

explanation.surface: A trawler crew learns manners while hauling in a big catch of herring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having gathered' signals the insertion; the IN goes just after the opening F.
explanation.definitionFit: A finishing school is a private college where young women were taught social graces and etiquette.

clue.text: Correspondence bird-like, might you say?

indicators.note: asks how a word might sound when spoken, signalling a sound-alike

parts.note: like a particular talking bird, a parrot, so jokingly parroty

explanation.surface: A question about whether letters can be described as resembling a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: The made-up adjective 'parroty' (like a parrot) is spoken to give the entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Correspondence in the sense of equivalence or matching one-to-one is parity.

clue.text: After a write-up, stop screening programme — put to bed again?

indicators.note: screening means hiding behind or within, so one word encloses the other
in a down clue, being written up means read from the bottom upward

parts.note: to deter is to stop or discourage
a programme is a plan of action

explanation.surface: A critic's review leads someone to pull a television programme off the schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'After a write-up' reads upward, giving RETED, which 'screening' wraps around the programme.
explanation.definitionFit: Flower beds: plants moved and set into a bed again have been planted afresh.

clue.text: Light texture's back in flesh

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: bacon is cured pig flesh

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter, here of texture's

explanation.surface: A cook notes the light texture of the back meat.
explanation.definitionFit: A beacon is a signal light or fire used as a guide or warning.

clue.text: Poor person's head hit

parts.note: bum is slang for poor or inferior

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, here of person's

explanation.surface: A down-and-out person suffers a blow to the head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor person' looks like one unit (a bum is a tramp), but BUM comes from 'Poor' alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to bump is to knock or strike against something.

clue.text: Church joining party once worried, not enjoying it?

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
Lib is the old Liberal party, now merged into the Liberal Democrats
something that ate at you worried you

explanation.surface: A churchgoer worried about joining a political party, and not enjoying the experience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' in the definition is the cheeky euphemism for sex.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone chaste abstains from sex, coyly called 'it', so is not enjoying that activity.

clue.text: Complaint, as leader punched by boy

indicators.note: punched by means pierced by, so the second piece goes inside the first

parts.note: Theresa May was a British Prime Minister and Conservative leader
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A complaint made when a political leader was punched by a youth.
explanation.walkthrough: Theresa May led the UK government from 2016 to 2019.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a complaint in the medical sense is an illness or disorder.

clue.text: Legitimate rubbish written about French here

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word wraps round the other

parts.note: offal is refuse or waste matter, as well as entrails
ici is the French word for here

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses as rubbish what has been written about the French in this country.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something legitimate is authorised or sanctioned, as an approved document is.

clue.text: Unexpected blow, one doing otherwise with drink

parts.note: one who sucks does the opposite of blowing, playing on the word blow in the definition
punch is a mixed drink

explanation.surface: A surprise blow struck by someone acting out of character after a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'otherwise' refers back to 'blow': the opposite of a blower is a sucker.
explanation.definitionFit: A sucker punch is a hit landed without warning on an unprepared victim.

clue.text: Covered in poo, water hardly in short supply to get hands cleaner?

indicators.note: covered in says one piece is wrapped around another

parts.note: manure is animal dung

indicators.note: in short means cut short, so the last letter is lost

parts.note: ice is hardly water: water made hard

explanation.surface: Someone covered in dung, with water scarce, needs something to clean their hands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'water hardly' is water made hard; 'in short supply' docks its last letter to leave IC, which 'Covered in' places inside the dung.
explanation.definitionFit: A manicure is a cosmetic treatment that tidies and cleans the hands and nails.

clue.text: Scorer with 22 in game, we hear?

indicators.note: we hear says the words are spoken, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: 22 down is a word sounding like seek, and in the children's game hide-and-seek the words before it are hide and

explanation.surface: A sports question about who scored when a certain player was in the game.
explanation.walkthrough: 22 is SIKH, which sounds like 'seek'; the game is hide-and-seek, and 'hide and' spoken aloud gives the composer's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A scorer here is one who writes musical scores, and Joseph Haydn was a classical composer.

clue.text: Fixed stocking material with a safety device

indicators.note: stocking means holding within, as a shop stocks goods, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: firm means fixed or secure
real means material or actual, as opposed to imagined

explanation.surface: Someone mended a pair of stockings made from fabric that came with a safety device.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stocking' and 'material' both pretend to be about hosiery.
explanation.definitionFit: A fire alarm is a device that warns occupants of a fire, a piece of safety equipment.

clue.text: Signed when joined, initial unnecessary

indicators.note: the first letter of the word is not needed and is dropped

parts.note: linked means joined

explanation.surface: A contract was signed at the point of joining, making the initial redundant.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to ink a deal is to sign it, so a signed contract has been inked.

clue.text: Young animal pulling tail from bird

indicators.note: removing the tail of a word takes off its last letter

parts.note: a kite is a bird of prey

explanation.surface: A young creature tugging feathers from a bird's tail.
explanation.definitionFit: A kit is the young of animals such as foxes, ferrets or beavers.

clue.text: Explosive stuff sent over, stronger tinderboxes?

indicators.note: sent over says the hidden letters are read backwards
stuff here is the contents of the boxes, so the letters are taken from inside the following words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Something explosive was shipped across: tougher boxes for kindling, perhaps?
explanation.walkthrough: The draft read 'Explosive stuff' as the definition, leaving the hiding unsignalled; 'stuff' is the filling of 'stronger tinderboxes', and 'Explosive' alone serves as a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Nitre is saltpetre, potassium nitrate, a key ingredient of gunpowder and so an explosive.

clue.text: Go without starter, standing to eat McDonald's after bar snack

indicators.note: to eat something is to take it inside, so one piece holds the other
in a down clue, standing means upright, so the letters read upwards
without its starter means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: to exit is to go out

indicators.note: after places the logo letter behind the bar

parts.note: a rail is a bar
M is the golden-arches logo of the McDonald's fast-food chain

explanation.surface: A hungry walker sets off, then stands eating a burger after a bar snack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without starter' leaves XIT, 'standing' reads it upward as TIX, and 'eat' wraps that around the bar plus the golden-arches letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Trail mix is a snack of nuts and dried fruit carried by hikers.

clue.text: Ultimately, muscle behind lift

indicators.note: ultimately points to the very last letter of the word muscle

parts.note: late means behind time

explanation.surface: In the end it is the muscles at the back that do the lifting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'muscle behind' reads like a phrase, but 'behind' is LATE on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: To lift someone's spirits is to cheer them up, which is what elate means as a verb.

clue.text: Sharp as Old King Cole in the end

parts.note: Tut is Tutankhamun, the ancient Egyptian boy king

indicators.note: in the end picks out the final letter of Cole

explanation.surface: The nursery-rhyme monarch Old King Cole turned out sharp in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old King Cole' is the nursery-rhyme merry old soul, but here 'Old King' is TUT and 'Cole' gives only its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone sharp is shrewd and quick-witted.

clue.text: Famous singer Ice-T, artist making comeback

parts.note: ice is rocks, as in a drink on the rocks, followed by the letter T

indicators.note: making a comeback means coming back, so the letters run in reverse

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: The rapper Ice-T, an artist, is staging a comeback.
explanation.walkthrough: Ice-T the rapper is a red herring: 'Ice' gives ROCKS and the T stays.
explanation.definitionFit: A rock star is a celebrated performer of rock music, a famous singer.

clue.text: Indian Arab chief, not he

indicators.note: not says the following word is left out

parts.note: a sheikh is an Arab leader

explanation.surface: An Indian Arab chief is said to be not a man.
explanation.definitionFit: Followers of Sikhism are mostly from the Punjab in India, so a Sikh is often Indian.

clue.text: Metal instrument, one probing stomach

parts.note: a lute is a stringed instrument

indicators.note: probing means poking into, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: tum is an informal word for the stomach
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A doctor's metal instrument, one used to probe the stomach.
explanation.definitionFit: Lutetium is a rare-earth metallic element, atomic number 71.

clue.text: So-called raw pepper

indicators.note: so-called says this is how the word is called out, a sound-alike

parts.note: raw weather is cold and damp, or chilly

explanation.surface: A pepper that is supposedly eaten uncooked.
explanation.definitionFit: A chilli is a small hot pepper of the capsicum family.

clue.text: Creator questionably needing time to influence past events

indicators.note: questionably means in a doubtful manner, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A creator, doubtfully, needs time to change history.
explanation.definitionFit: To act retrospectively is to have an effect on things already done or passed.

clue.text: Clean tongue

definitions.meaning: to shine or clean by rubbing
a tongue is a language, here the language of Poland

explanation.surface: Clean tongue
explanation.definitionFit: Polish is both a verb meaning to make shine and the language spoken in Poland.
